items.passage: Transcript: Hi, this is Oluwaseun Brandt from campus transportation. While Garner Road is being repaved, two shuttle routes change. Normally every route picks up at the main gate on College Avenue. During the repaving, the evening loop will pick up at the stadium parking lot instead, on the side facing the tennis courts. The morning express is moving too, but not to the stadium; for these two weeks it'll use the circle in front of the library. The night safe-ride van isn't affected and still stops outside the health centre. Now, some of you got an email saying all of this starts Monday. That email went out a little too early. We'd planned on Monday, but the paving crew pushed back their start, so nothing changes until Wednesday. The stops listed in that message are still correct.
items.prompt: [Announcement — Campus shuttle service] Why does the speaker say, "That email went out a little too early"?
choices: To explain why some riders have the wrong start date
To warn riders that the email had listed the wrong stops
To tell riders to disregard everything in the email
To explain why the route changes have been called off
items.correct_answer: To explain why some riders have the wrong start date
items.explanation: The email said the changes start Monday; the speaker then explains, "the paving crew pushed back their start, so nothing changes until Wednesday." The remark accounts for the wrong date. "To warn riders that the email had listed the wrong stops" and "To tell riders to disregard everything in the email" are contradicted by "The stops listed in that message are still correct." "To explain why the route changes have been called off" is wrong because the changes still happen, starting Wednesday.
